newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Ortega refuses to recognise Nicaragua results.
newsitem.headline: Ortega refuses to recognise Nicaragua results.

text.p: Sandinista candidate Daniel Ortega refused on Monday to recognise partial official results in Nicaragua's presidential election that gave his right-wing rival Arnoldo Aleman victory, saying election officials should re-check their numbers.

"What we are saying is that they should carry out a count...based on the (voting) acts," Ortega told reporters. "On this occasion we would have liked to have recognised (the results) but we feel we cannot."
Ortega claimed that the Sandinistas had found "serious irregularities" including alterations in telegrams of voting figures sent by polling stations to the Supreme Electoral Council's headquarters.
"Many of these telegrams don't reflect the number of votes", he said. After Ortega spoke, a small group of Sandinista supporters outside his campaign headquarters shouted angrily for new elections.

Ortega, Nicaragua's revolutionary president from 1979-90, also complained of problems in the northern state of Matagalpa, where he said other political parties as well as the Sandinistas had decided to contest the entire electoral process in that area.

Seeking to paint himself as a democrat, Ortega said he had readily accepted defeat in Nicaragua's last elections in 1990 but added that this time round he could not because of the irregularities. Election observers from the Organisation of American States and the European Union said on Sunday night that the vote had been legitimate despite some delays and administrative glitches.
